_README: Labelled 2026-10-12 by inspecting sampled frames from each clip.
HONEST STATE OF THIS SET: every clip is a NEGATIVE. There is not one frame of anyone in
difficulty, so RECALL CANNOT BE MEASURED from this data and must not be reported.
What this set CAN measure, and measure well, is the false-alarm rate on real coastal CCTV -
which is the number that decides whether lifeguards would keep the system switched on.
Times are seconds. 'distress': [] means nothing in the clip should raise an event.
'zone' is normalised (0..1, origin top-left); omit for the whole frame.

clips.notes: THE important clip. 24.5 min of fixed elevated coastal webcam, 480x360, real surf and real crowds. Correct deployment geometry. Zone covers the water band only, so promenade and road traffic are excluded. Primary false-alarm benchmark.
Crowded beach, handheld. 157 track ids for 32 people - the clip that exposed the fragmentation problem. Keep as a tracking-stability regression.
Kovalam, scenic wide. A few people in distant surf. Weak negative - very few water users.
Sunset shoreline, one person walking. Weak negative.
Lighthouse headland. Almost no people in water.
Vertical phone video, sunset silhouettes on wet sand. Tests the vertical-posture signal against people who are upright and perfectly fine.
Vertical, waves only, no people. Pure false-positive probe: any event here is the detector firing on foam.
Fishermen and a boat at the waterline. Standing figures near water - another upright-but-fine probe.
Sunset, moored boat, empty. Low light - probes the detector on poor contrast.
